'''Jacqueline Anne''' "'''Jackie'''" '''Stedall''' (4 August 1950 – 27 September 2014)<ref name=Guardian>{{cite news| url= https://www.theguardian.com/education/2014/oct/24/jacqueline-stedall| title= Jacqueline Stedall obituary| last=Neumann| first=Peter| work=[[The Guardian]]| date=24 October 2014| accessdate=23 October 2016}}</ref> was a British [[history of mathematics|mathematics historian]]. She wrote nine books,<ref name=Guardian /> and appeared on radio on [[BBC Radio 4]]'s ''[[In Our Time (radio series)|In Our Time]]'' programme.

== Early life ==
Stedall was born in [[Romford]], [[Essex]], and attended [[Queen Mary's High School]] in [[Walsall]].<ref name=Guardian /> Her academic achievements included a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in [[mathematics]] from [[Girton College, Cambridge]], an [[Master of Science|MSc]] in [[statistics]] from the [[University of Kent]], a [[Professional Graduate Certificate in Education|PGCE]] from [[Bristol Polytechnic]] (now the [[University of the West of England]]), and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in the [[history of mathematics]] from the [[Open University]].<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Ox>{{cite news| url= https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/12994| title= Jacqueline Anne Stedall (4 August 1950 – 27 September 2014)| work=[[University of Oxford]]| date=1 October 2014| accessdate=23 October 2016}}</ref> Her PhD focused upon [[John Wallis]]' 1685 work ''Treatise of Algebra''.<ref name=BSHM>{{cite journal| type=pdf| title= Subverting expectations: memories of editing with Jackie| volume=30| issue=3| journal=[[British Society for the History of Mathematics]]| pages=178–182| last=Robson| first=Eleanor| author-link=Eleanor Robson| date=27 October 2015| doi=10.1080/17498430.2015.1055902| s2cid= 123529423| url=http://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1476497/1/remembering_jackie_rev.pdf}}</ref>

== Career ==
After her MSc degree, Stedall worked for three years as a [[statistician]] at the [[University of Bristol]], and four years as an administrator for [[War on Want]]. Subsequently, she worked as a [[teacher]] for eight years.<ref name=Ox /> Stedall's academic career began in 2000, when she became a Clifford Norton student at [[The Queen's College, Oxford]], studying the history of science.<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Ox /> She later became a [[fellow]] of the college, and created a third-year module on the history of mathematics at the University of Oxford.<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Ox /> In 2002, Stedall became the managing editor of the [[British Society for the History of Mathematics]]'s newsletter, which later became the [[BSHM Bulletin]] journal. She worked alongside fellow mathematical historian [[Eleanor Robson]].<ref name=BSHM /> 

Stedall appeared multiple times on the [[BBC Radio 4]] programme ''[[In Our Time (radio series)|In Our Time]]''. Topics that she discussed on the programme included [[Archimedes]], whether [[Isaac Newton]] or [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz]] were the founder of [[calculus]], the [[Fibonacci sequence]], [[prime number]]s in finance, and [[Renaissance]] era mathematics.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~jcollins/OpenStudies/links.html| title=Mathematical ideas that shaped the world| last1=Collins| first1=Julia| last2=Docherty| first2=Pamela| publisher=maths.ed.ac.uk| accessdate=23 October 2016| url-status=dead| archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721114750/http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~jcollins/OpenStudies/links.html| archivedate=21 July 2015| df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4tlqiPdbKmEC&q=jackie+stedall| title=In Our Time: A companion to the Radio 4 series| last=Bragg| first=Melvyn| publisher=[[Hachette UK]]| date=December 2011| access-date=23 October 2016| isbn=978-1-4447-4285-5}}</ref>

==Books==
Stedall wrote a 2008 book ''Mathematics Emerging''<ref name="Guinness2010">{{cite journal|last1=Grattan Guinness|first1=I.|authorlink=Ivor Grattan-Guinness|title=Review of ''Mathematics Emerging. A Sourcebook 1540–1900''|journal=Annals of Science|volume=68|issue=1|year=2010|pages=133–134|issn=0003-3790|doi=10.1080/00033790802657848|s2cid=121561644}}</ref> which was used as the primary textbook for her course.<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Ox />
She also co-edited and published the ''Oxford Handbook of the History of Mathematics''.<ref name=Telegraph />
With [[Janet Beery]], she co-edited ''[[De numeris triangularibus et inde de progressionibus arithmeticis: Magisteria magna|Thomas Harriot’s Doctrine of Triangular Numbers: the 'Magisteria Magna']]'' (European Mathematical Society, 2009).<ref>Reviews of ''Thomas Harriot’s Doctrine of Triangular Numbers'':
*{{cite web|date=March 2009|title=Review|work=MAA Reviews|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/thomas-harriots-doctrine-of-triangular-numbers-the-magisteria-magna|first=Fernando Q.|last=Gouvêa|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|access-date=2025-07-28}}
*{{cite journal|title=Before calculus|first=Matthias|last=Schemmel|journal=Notes and Records of the Royal Society of London|volume=64|issue=3|date=September 2010|pages=303–304|jstor=20753908|doi=10.1098/rsnr.2010.0016|doi-access=free}}
*{{cite journal|year=2010|title=none|first=William R.|last=Shea|journal=Mathematical Reviews|mr=2516550}}
*{{cite journal|url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/thomas-harriots-doctrine-triangular-numbers-magisteria-magna|journal=European Mathematical Society Reviews|date=May 2011|title=Review|archive-date=19 November 2018|access-date=19 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119132948/http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/thomas-harriots-doctrine-triangular-numbers-magisteria-magna|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2012, Stedall wrote the book ''[[The History of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction]]'', part of the [[Oxford University Press]]' ''Very Short Introduction'' series of books. The book focused on "what mathematical historians do and how they do it".<ref>Reviews of ''The History of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction'':
*{{cite journal | last = Blanco | first = Mònica | journal = Actes d'História de la Ciència i de la Técnica | language = ca | pages = 161–163 | title = Review | url = https://www.raco.cat/index.php/ActesHistoria/article/download/91053/401406 | volume = 8 | year = 2015}}
*{{cite web | last = Ferguson | first = Wallace A. | date = June 2013 | publisher = Institute of Mathematics and its Applications | title = Review | url = https://ima.org.uk/421/the-history-of-introduction/ | work = IMA Reviews}}
*{{cite web| url= http://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-history-of-mathematics-a-very-short-introduction| title= Review| last=Gouvêa| first=Fernando Q.|authorlink= Fernando Q. Gouvêa |work=MAA Reviews |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]| date=21 December 2012| accessdate=23 October 2016}}
*{{cite journal|first=Leon|last=Harkleroad|journal=MathSciNet|title=Review of ''The History of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction''|mr=3137003}}
*{{cite journal|first=Franz|last=Lemmermeyer|journal=zbMATH|title=Review of ''The History of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction''|zbl=1244.00001}}
*{{cite journal | last = Leversha | first = Gerry | date = March 2014 | doi = 10.1017/s0025557200000917 | issue = 541 | journal = The Mathematical Gazette | jstor = 24496613 | pages = 155–156 | title = none | volume = 98| s2cid = 233360256 }}
*{{cite journal | last = Schneebeli | first = H. R. | doi = 10.4171/EM/231 | issue = 3 | journal = [[Elemente der Mathematik]] | language = de | page = 136 | title = Review of ''The History of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction'' | volume = 68 | year = 2013| doi-access = free }}
*{{cite journal | last = Sonar | first = Thomas | date = September 2014 | doi = 10.1080/17498430.2014.920217 | issue = 3 | journal = BSHM Bulletin: Journal of the British Society for the History of Mathematics | pages = 217–219 | title = none | volume = 29| s2cid = 120118503 }}
</ref> It won the 2013 [[Peter M. Neumann|Neumann Prize]] for the best English-language book on the history of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.bshm.ac.uk/neumann-prize| title= Neumann Prize| publisher=[[British Society for the History of Mathematics]]| accessdate=2 November 2016}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Stedall was married and had two children.<ref name=Telegraph />

Whilst suffering from [[cancer]], Stedall joined the Painswick Friends' meeting house, which "helped her find peace with her illness".<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Telegraph>{{cite news| url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/law-and-order/11686151/Terminally-ill-Oxford-research-fellow-targeted-by-Romanian-fraudster.html| title= Terminally ill Oxford research fellow targeted by Romanian fraudster| work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]| date=19 June 2015| accessdate=23 October 2016}}</ref> In March 2014, she was robbed by a Romanian fraud gang, who stole her bank card.<ref name=Telegraph />

Stedall died of cancer on 27 September 2014.<ref name=Guardian /><ref name=Ox /> In her will, she donated money to [[The Queen's College, Oxford|Queen's College]] Library for the preservation of mathematical history books.<ref>{{cite journal| url=http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/sites/www.queens.ox.ac.uk/files/Insight2015.pdf| type=pdf| title=From the Librarian| issue=5| journal=Insight| publisher=Queen's College Oxford Library| pages=1,2,6| date=2015| accessdate=2 November 2016| archive-date=24 April 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424195741/http://www.queens.ox.ac.uk/sites/www.queens.ox.ac.uk/files/Insight2015.pdf| url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015, the [[Canadian Society for History and Philosophy of Mathematics]] held a special session to remember Stedall, and in 2016, the [[British Society for the History of Mathematics]] held a two-day meeting at Queen's College on sixteenth- and seventeenth-century algebra, which they dedicated to Stedall.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://historyofmathematics.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/CallforPapersMathFest2015.pdf| type=pdf| title=Call for Papers| work=[[Canadian Society for History and Philosophy of Mathematics]] | date=2015| accessdate=2 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.bshm.ac.uk/events/mathematics-emerging-tribute-jackie-stedall-and-her-influence-history-mathematics| title= Mathematics emerging: A tribute to Jackie Stedall and her influence on the history of mathematics| publisher=[[British Society for the History of Mathematics]]| accessdate=23 October 2016}}</ref>
